text: Paul, a servant of God and an apostle of Jesus Christ for the faith of God's chosen ones and the knowledge of the truth that leads to godliness,
resting on the hope of eternal life, which God, who does not lie, promised before the ages began
and at the proper time he revealed his word through the preaching entrusted to me by the command of God our Savior:

versions.text: and revealed at the proper time in his word through the preaching entrusted to me by the command of God our Savior:
versions.explanation: τὸν λόγον αὐτοῦ is the direct object of ἐφανέρωσεν ("he revealed his word"), not a locative phrase. Rendering it "in his word" leaves the verb without an object and obscures the sense that God's word itself was made manifest through the proclamation.

text: To Titus, my true son in our common faith. Grace and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Savior.
I left you in Crete for this reason: that you might set right what still needed to be done and appoint elders in every town, as I directed you.
An elder must be beyond reproach, the husband of one wife, with children who are believers and not open to the charge of wild living or rebellion.
For as God's steward, an overseer must be beyond reproach: not arrogant, not quick-tempered, not given to drink, not violent, not greedy for dishonest gain,
but hospitable, a lover of what is good, self-controlled, upright, holy, and disciplined.
He must hold firmly to the trustworthy word as it has been taught, so that he can encourage others with sound doctrine and refute those who oppose it.
For there are many rebellious people, empty talkers and deceivers, especially those of the circumcision group.
They must be silenced, because they are ruining whole households by teaching what they should not teach—and all for the sake of dishonest gain.
One of them, a prophet of their own people, said: "Cretans are always liars, vicious brutes, lazy gluttons."

versions.text: One of their own, a prophet of their very own, said it: "Cretans are always liars, vicious brutes, lazy gluttons."
versions.explanation: "One of their own, a prophet of their very own" doubles the same English wording awkwardly, and "said it" is an unnatural addition. The revision keeps the Greek's emphasis on "their own" prophet while reading more smoothly aloud.

text: This testimony is true. So rebuke them sharply, that they may be sound in the faith
and pay no attention to Jewish myths or to the commands of people who turn their backs on the truth.
To the pure, everything is pure; but to those who are defiled and unbelieving, nothing is pure. In fact, both their minds and their consciences are defiled.
They claim to know God, but by their actions they deny him. They are detestable, disobedient, and unfit for any good work.

versions.text: They claim to know God, but by their actions they deny him. They are detestable, disobedient, and unfit for anything good.
versions.explanation: ἔργον ("work, deed") is dropped in "anything good." The point is unfitness for good works, which also mirrors the contrast with their "actions" (ἔργοις) earlier in the verse.

versions.text: They are detestable, disobedient, and unfit for any good work.
versions.explanation: The opening clause θεὸν ὁμολογοῦσιν εἰδέναι, τοῖς δὲ ἔργοις ἀρνοῦνται ("They claim to know God, but by their actions they deny him") was dropped in a previous revision. It must be restored; without it the participle "being" (ὄντες) has no governing statement and the contrast between profession and deeds is lost. The earlier correction of "anything good" to "any good work" is retained.
